tagline.text: A quiet dive island off Loon, Bohol, known for coral walls and hammerhead sharks

location.label: Location
location.text: Off the coast of Loon, Bohol (Cebu Strait, about 8 km west of the Loon mainland)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Dry season, December–May (hammerhead sharks around January–April)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: From about ₱1,500–3,500 (per night, room only; some resorts US$60–120 or more; diving extra — check locally)

children.text: Cabilao Island is a small island a few kilometers around, floating off Loon on the main island of Bohol. Along its west coast, coral walls, giant sea fans and macro life make it a well-known dive destination. In winter you may even meet hammerhead sharks, and with almost no cars the whole island is peaceful.
Cabilao Island lies in the Cebu Strait west of mainland Bohol and belongs administratively to the municipality of Loon in Bohol Province. Sources put its area at roughly

, and the 2020 census counted about 4,600 residents. The island has five barangays: Cabacongan, Cambaquiz, Looc, Pantudlan and Talisay. Residents make a living mainly from fishing, farming and tourism.

The island is famous for its sea. Around 15 dive sites are said to ring the island, and the seven or so on the west coast, from Lighthouse Point to South Point, are considered the best stretch. Giant sea fans and soft corals cling to sheer coral walls, while the sandy areas are dotted with coral heads, so you can enjoy both big animals and tiny macro life in one trip.

The atmosphere is nothing like Panglao's busy beaches. The island is separated from the mainland, so there is no bridge and almost no cars; most getting around is by motorcycle or tricycle. The few resorts cluster on the west coast, so evenings are left to the sound of waves and the stars. For divers it is an easy place to focus on the sea all day, and non-divers can still snorkel, stroll through villages and visit the lake and lighthouse.

Keep in mind that getting here takes some effort and that the small number of resorts limits your choices. Day trips for diving from Panglao exist, but the travel time is long, so you really need to stay at least one night to appreciate the island. This guide is based on publicly available sources, and boat fares and resort operating status change often, so check the latest information before you book.

blocks.title: Coral walls on the west coast

children.text: The west coast offers wall dives that drop steeply from shallow coral into deeper water. Between the walls there are large sea fans, soft corals and cave-like crevices, so there is something to look at wherever you turn. This stretch is the heart of Cabilao diving.
Around January to April, hammerhead sharks are said to come up from deep water near the lighthouse and off the northwest point. Your chances are reportedly best on the first dive at dawn (about
), but a sighting is never guaranteed. Go expecting that the walls and coral scenery alone will be satisfying even if you miss them.

Nudibranchs, frogfish, pygmy seahorses and other small creatures are plentiful, which is why macro divers like to come here. The sandy areas, coral heads and the house reef are all good places to search. Guides often find seahorses and nudibranchs for you, so tell them your macro interests in advance.
At the southern tip of the island, South Point has an overhanging wall that drops to about

below a shallow rock ledge, and it is regarded as a challenging dive. Recreational dives usually run along the wall at shallower depths, so discuss a plan that fits your certification and experience with your guide.

The house reef, which you enter straight from the resort beach, is used for check dives, relaxed daytime dives, night dives and training. The shallow reef flat on the east side of the island is described as snorkelable from the beach without a boat. A rash guard or wetsuit gives peace of mind against jellyfish and other stinging animals.

At Punta Baluarte on the island's northwest side, a small museum stands in the restored ruins of a Spanish-era lighthouse, alongside an old lighthouse, a modern lighthouse and the foundations of a Spanish-era stone watchtower. It makes a good loop on a rest day between dives.

Near Pantudlan in the island's interior is Cabilao Island Lake (also called Lake Lanao), known as the only natural lake in Bohol, with mangroves and birds. Bird hunting is prohibited, and the island is described as having more bird species than anywhere else in Bohol. The path to the observation huts may be poor, so ask a local about conditions before you go.

Residents of Pantudlan weave mats, hats and bags (bayong) from pandanus leaves and sell them. Walk into the village between dives to watch the weaving and buy a souvenir, which directly helps local people.

items.title: 1 night 2 days diving course
items.subtitle: From Panglao to the island, two or three dives

children.text: Leave Panglao and head toward Loon. A resort car or rental car is the easiest way; by public transport, take a van or bus bound for Loon from the Tagbilaran bus terminal.
Arrive at Mocpoc Pier on the Loon coast. From here a bangka takes about
30–45 minutes
to cross to Cabilao Island.
Check in at the resort and make your first dive. Checking your buoyancy and equipment on the house reef is the safe way to start.
After lunch, make a second dive at a west-coast wall site. Around sunset, relax on the beach or walk through the village.
Watch the sunset, have dinner and turn in early. There is almost no nightlife on the island.

On the second morning there is a dawn first dive aimed at hammerhead sharks, and it is common to return to Loon after the morning dive. Do not cut your flight or boat connections too tight; leave some margin.

items.title: Half-day course for non-divers
items.subtitle: Snorkeling, then a walk to the villages and lighthouse

children.text: Arrive on the island by bangka and leave your bags at the resort.
Snorkel from the beach. Wear a long-sleeved rash guard to protect against jellyfish and sun.
Have lunch and rest at the resort restaurant.
Tour the Punta Baluarte lighthouse museum and Pantudlan village by motorcycle or tricycle.
Take a bangka back to Loon. Book the return boat in advance.
A day trip is possible, but boat transfers and the round trip from Panglao take a lot of time and make the day tight. If possible, stay one night.
There are direct flights from Manila to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG). Flight schedules change by season, so check when you book.
You can also fly to Cebu and cross to Tagbilaran by a ferry such as OceanJet.

items.title: Boat from Loon to the island

children.text: From the Loon mainland or Mocpoc at the western tip of Sandingan Island, the bangka ride takes about
30–45 minutes
The scheduled public bangka to Talisay Pier costs about
, but reports say it waits until about 16 passengers board, so timing is irregular. A chartered bangka is about
one way, and a bangka that goes straight to the resort is reported at about
The resorts are on the island's west coast while the public pier is on the opposite side, so if you land at the public pier you still need a motorcycle or tricycle to reach your resort.
Boat times and fares change with waves and tides. The surest option is to ask your resort to book your transport before you arrive.
There are almost no cars on the island, and motorcycles and tricycles are the main transport. Walking between resorts is also common.
There are reports that the island has no ATM, so bring plenty of cash.

Diving is said to be possible all year. May to October is the resort low season and some resorts reduce operations, though some say this does not affect dive quality. December to May is Bohol's dry season, when the weather is steady and boat conditions are generally good.
The hammerhead season is described differently by different sources, such as about
January–April
or
December–June
. Either way, a sighting is not guaranteed, so if sharks are your goal, plan a stay of several days with multiple dawn dives.

Accommodation centers on dive resorts along the west coast. Cabilao Sunset Dive & Beach Resort is described as run by a German owner for more than 20 years, and divers step from the beach straight onto the dive boat. Polaris and Cabilao Sanctuary and a few others are also known, but one July 2025 visit report said some resorts appeared to be running with only minimal staff or almost closed, so be sure to confirm that a resort is operating before booking. There is also lodging in Cambaquiz in the northeast of the island.

Most meals are taken at the resort restaurant. Many resorts sell rooms as packages that include meals and diving, so you rarely need to look for a restaurant. There are few shops on the island, so bring snacks, bottled water and personal medicines from Panglao or Tagbilaran. An older source mentions that electricity in some places comes from a generator, so schedule charging of your equipment for the hours when the resort has power.
If you are aiming for hammerhead sharks, book the dawn first dive (about
) and plan to stay at least 2–3 days. Sharks are not guaranteed.
The west-coast wall sites are deep and may have currents. With Advanced certification or above you have more choices; with Open Water, ask for shallower sites.
The island is said to have no ATM, so withdraw plenty of cash in Panglao or Tagbilaran and ask in advance whether lodging and dive fees can be paid by card.
Boats are affected by waves and tides. Leave at least a day of margin before an international flight or ferry rather than leaving the island on the same afternoon.
When chartering a bangka, agree on departure time, return time and fare in advance and check that life jackets are worn.
When snorkeling, wear a long-sleeved rash guard or wetsuit against jellyfish and sun.
If you shoot macro photos, tell your guide your target creatures in advance. Seahorses and nudibranchs are hard to find unless you know where they are.
Choose a resort based on recent reviews. Some resorts close or reduce operations in the low season.
The west-coast wall sites are deep and may have currents. Choose sites that suit your certification and experience, and follow your guide's instructions and your dive plan.
A hammerhead sighting is never guaranteed, and the season length differs by source. Do not plan your trip around sharks alone.
I could not confirm any marine sanctuary fee from an official source. When booking, ask the resort whether it is included in the total.
Do not touch or step on corals and marine life. If your buoyancy control is shaky, practice in shallow water and keep clear of the coral.

Emergency medical facilities on the island are limited. Check your dive insurance (such as DAN) and travel insurance, and agree in advance with the resort how to get to the mainland quickly if something goes wrong.
Bangkas may not leave in bad weather. In typhoon season, check cancellation and change conditions.
The path to the lake observation huts on the northwest side may be in poor condition. It can be slippery after rain, so ask a local first.
Panglao Island
, with its airport and many resorts, is the gateway to Cabilao, about
1.5–2 hours
away by car.
Balicasag Island
is a diving and snorkeling spot off Panglao that is often combined with Cabilao on a Bohol diving itinerary.
Tagbilaran City
, Bohol's port city, is about
40 km
from Loon and is the gateway where Cebu ferries arrive.
Loboc River
is a scenic attraction in the same western direction as Loon, so it can be fitted in along the way.
